ak-context-engineering.tagline: Manage context, budgets, compaction, and model choice from evidence.
ak-context-engineering.summary: ak:context-engineering finishes the right work with the least wasted context, cost, and steps, never by cutting scope or verification. It returns grounded advice, a state checkpoint, or numbers from offline analysis scripts.
howItWorks: Frames outcome and acceptance, then reads runtime telemetry; missing values stay unknown, never estimated.
Context bands: Green <50%, Yellow 50–<70%, Orange 70–<85%, Red ≥85%; Orange triggers checkpoint then compaction.
Compares models on matched tasks by cost, duration, first-attempt cost, and steps; never switches models automatically.
Delegates only when isolation outweighs startup cost; packets include paths, acceptance, budget, and stop condition.
Merges checkpoints into existing plans/notes; offline scripts: context_analyzer.py, compression_evaluator.py, benchmark_metrics.py.
useWhen: A long session slows down, forgets decisions, or runs low on context.
Deciding whether and how to split work across subagents.
Comparing cost, time, or steps across models on the same tasks.
avoidWhen: Short tasks with no context problem.
Handing a session to another agent: use ak:handoff.
Benchmarking models on DeepSWE: use ak:deep-swe.

params.name: [topic or question]
params.desc: Context or budget question: token waste, remaining context, compaction, model choice, delegation, memory, or compression.

examples.cmd: /ak:context-engineering how much context is left in this session, and should I checkpoint?
examples.note: Assesses headroom and decides on checkpoint/compaction.

examples.cmd: /ak:context-engineering should this refactor be split across 3 subagents?
examples.note: Weighs delegation cost against inline work.

tips: Without telemetry, record unknown; never turn tool-call counts into a context percentage.
Batching commands saves turns but adds no context capacity; still cap total output.
Fix deterministic errors before retrying; use backoff only for transient ones.
artifacts: Checkpoint merged into an existing plan or note

ak-handoff.tagline: Write a redacted continuation file for a fresh agent; optionally dispatch it.
ak-handoff.summary: ak:handoff writes a 9-section Markdown contract to plans/handoffs/<slug>-<YYYYMMDD-HHmm>.md and prints its path. With --dispatch --agent <id>, it validates the file and hands one job to ak:orchestrate on your chosen runtime.
howItWorks: Runs read-only git probes; --include-diff and --include-status add bounded, redacted diff and status.
Writes 9 sections, from mission to exact next actions, starting with a First safe step; gaps say 'Not captured'.
Redacts keys, tokens, passwords, .env values, and personal data; refuses to overwrite without --force.
--dispatch validates the file, writes plans/reports/orchestrate-<timestamp>/jobs.yaml, and calls ak:orchestrate.
Dispatched jobs default to scoped writes, approval required, worktree isolation, and a 10-minute timeout.
useWhen: Context is running out and the next session must continue without rediscovery.
Moving work to another runtime (Codex, Cursor, OpenCode) with --dispatch --agent <id>.
Sending an existing handoff file to another runtime with --dispatch --handoff PATH.
avoidWhen: Human status report from branches and plans: use ak:watzup.
Parallel multi-runtime work with an arbiter: use ak:orchestrate.
Recapping results for people: use ak:sumup.

params.name: [task focus]
params.desc: Focus for the next agent; also the file slug. Credentials are refused.

params.name: --output PATH
params.desc: Explicit artifact path inside the workspace.

params.name: --include-diff
params.desc: Adds git diff --stat and the first 200 diff lines, redacted.

params.name: --include-status
params.desc: Adds a redacted git status --short snapshot.

params.name: --force
params.desc: Allows overwriting an existing artifact; not implied by --output.

params.name: --dispatch
params.desc: Validates the handoff and dispatches one job via ak:orchestrate.

params.name: --agent <id>
params.desc: Required with --dispatch; no default. E.g. claude-code, codex, internal, opencode, cursor; unknown IDs are refused.

params.name: --handoff PATH
params.desc: Reuses an existing handoff instead of capturing; it must pass schema and redaction checks.

params.name: --cwd PATH
params.desc: Workspace root for the dispatched job; defaults to the current workspace.

params.name: --model NAME
params.desc: Overrides the model for CLI runtime jobs; refused with --agent internal.

params.name: --yes
params.desc: Approves writes in the dispatched job; never covers destructive changes.

params.name: --task TEXT
params.desc: Alternative to the positional focus with --dispatch; the positional wins if both are given.

examples.note: Writes only the continuation contract with a clear focus.
Captures, then dispatches to Claude Code via orchestrate with approval: require.
Reuses an existing handoff without a new capture.

tips: The next session should verify Current state against the repo before acting.
There is no fallback agent: a missing or unauthenticated runtime returns a blocker, and the file is kept.
Bypass flags like --dangerously-skip-permissions or --yolo are never added; specs with them are refused.

ak-journal.tagline: Write chronological technical journal entries via `ak journal create`.
ak-journal.summary: ak:journal records a session's root cause, changes, impact, decisions, and next steps as plans/journals/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md. It runs automatically at the end of ak:plan, ak:cook, ak:fix, ak:ship, and ak:bootstrap.
howItWorks: Collects key facts and writes a short entry, favoring specific errors, paths, and results.
Saves via ak journal create "<title>" --summary "<one-line>" --stdin; validates with ak journal validate.
Can use the journal-writer subagent for candid failure write-ups.
Skips AgentWiki publishing; the local file is canonical. Social posts need an explicit request and preview.
useWhen: You just fixed a hard bug and want the root cause recorded.
End of session: saving decisions and lessons on a timeline.
An approach failed and you want to analyze why later.
avoidWhen: Long-lived architecture decisions: use ADRs via ak:docs.
Handing work to another agent: use ak:handoff.
Git-metric retros: use ak:retro.

params.name: [topic or reflection]
params.desc: Topic or reflection for the entry. Empty summarizes the current session.

examples.note: Journals the session just completed.

examples.cmd: /ak:journal failed Postgres migration and how we rolled back
examples.note: Focuses on one specific incident.

tips: Disable auto-journal with --skip-journal or `ak config prefs set journal.auto false`; an explicit /ak:journal always runs.
Duplicate filenames get -2, -3 suffixes.
Browse entries with ak journal list / ak journal show <slug>.

ak-orchestrate.tagline: Run staged or parallel jobs across verified runtimes, Pi sessions, and subagents.
ak-orchestrate.summary: ak:orchestrate turns a task or YAML spec into a job graph and routes each job by capability and risk using live evidence. Parallel writers get worktrees, runs are resumable, and an independent arbiter reviews results before plans/reports/orchestrate-<timestamp>/report.md.
howItWorks: Builds jobs.yaml; same-stage jobs run in parallel only without file overlap.
Builds a live runtime inventory and routes via model-routing.md; no qualifying runtime means blocked.
Onboards a named but missing runtime such as Pi visibly; you do the auth step yourself.
Safety gate confirms cwd, writable roots, and side effects; bypass modes stay off; each process has a timeout.
After all jobs settle, a separate arbiter from another model family checks results; report.md records routes and verdict.
useWhen: Researching several options in parallel, then comparing them.
Getting an independent review from a different model family.
Repeatable staged work (scout → implement → review) or resuming an interrupted run.
avoidWhen: Simple single-agent tasks: orchestration only adds cost.
Handing the session to one agent: use ak:handoff --dispatch --agent <id>.
Teams that message each other: use ak:team.

params.name: <job-spec.yaml>
params.desc: Path to a repeatable YAML job spec (schema in references/job-spec.md).

params.name: <task description>
params.desc: Free-form request; writes jobs.yaml before dispatch. Naming a runtime (e.g. "as pi sessions") adds it and onboards it if missing.

params.name: --resume <run-dir>
params.desc: Continues an existing run; reconciles existing attempts and never blindly relaunches ones of unknown state.

params.name: --yes
params.desc: Approves actions within the spec's scope; out-of-scope actions still prompt (not documented in source).

params.name: --internal
params.desc: Prefers in-session subagents for unpinned jobs; not a hard mode and never overrides pinned routes.

examples.cmd: /ak:orchestrate "research three implementation options and compare them"
examples.note: Researches 3 options in parallel; the arbiter compares them.

examples.cmd: /ak:orchestrate "run the three scouts as pi sessions, then one arbiter"
examples.note: Scouts run as Pi sessions; Pi is onboarded first if missing or unauthenticated.
Runs an approved, repeatable spec.

tips: Worktrees prevent edit conflicts but are not sandboxes; lockfiles, migrations, and shared config run serially.
A silent process is not necessarily hung; wait for all_settled.
Pi onboarding never handles your API keys; headless Pi has no per-action approval, so avoid destructive jobs.

ak-team.tagline: Run parallel teammate sessions led by a coordinator with shared state.
ak-team.summary: ak:team builds a multi-session agent team from 4 templates: research, cook, review, debug. The lead splits work, spawns teammates, integrates, and verifies; it stops if the runtime lacks team support.
howItWorks: Checks the live collaboration surface; stops with an error instead of falling back to plain subagents.
Splits work into independent items with acceptance criteria and file ownership; picks the smallest team.
Templates: research (one angle each), cook (non-overlapping files), review (one focus each), debug (one hypothesis each).
With plan approval on, teammates stay read-only until the lead approves their plan.
Verifies merged results, shuts teammates down gracefully, then reports and runs /ak:journal.
useWhen: You have 3 or more independent workstreams.
Debugging with several competing hypotheses.
Parallel multi-angle review: security, performance, tests, architecture.
avoidWhen: A single test, lint, or review pass: use a plain subagent.
Sequential plan → code → test: use ak:cook.
Tight budget: each teammate has its own context and cost.

params.name: <template>
params.desc: One of research, cook, review, debug.

params.name: <context>
params.desc: Task description or plan path for the team.

params.name: --devs N
params.desc: Number of developer teammates (cook template).

params.name: --researchers N
params.desc: Number of researcher teammates (research template).

params.name: --reviewers N
params.desc: Number of reviewer teammates (review template).

params.name: --debuggers N
params.desc: Number of debugger teammates (debug template).

params.name: --delegate
params.desc: Lead only coordinates and reports; it edits no files.

params.name: --plan-approval / --no-plan-approval
params.desc: Turns the implementation plan approval gate on or off before teammates may write.

params.name: --worktree
params.desc: Requires isolated worktrees for implementation teammates.

examples.note: Parallel implementation from a plan with worktrees and plan approval.

examples.cmd: /ak:team debug "random request timeouts at the API gateway" --debuggers 3 --delegate
examples.note: Several hypotheses; the lead only coordinates.

tips: Pick the smallest team of truly independent workstreams.
Worktrees do not replace ownership; each teammate owns its own files.
For a stuck teammate, give specific guidance; if still stuck, hand off and reassign.
artifacts: Report or plan per work item

ak-sumup.tagline: Recap implemented work: results, failures, decisions, usage, follow-ups.
ak-sumup.summary: ak:sumup explains results, evidence, trade-offs, and remaining work without replaying the session. It is read-only and never claims a deploy without evidence.
howItWorks: Gathers evidence: conversation, decisions, current diff, tests, and issue or plan status.
Separates verified work from proposed, untested, or unshipped items.
Writes Outcome, Highlights, Failures and recovery, Decisions, How it works, How to use it, Follow-ups.
Drops empty sections, adds diagrams only when they clarify, and lists unresolved items last.
useWhen: A feature just finished and a reviewer or manager needs a recap.
You want to know what failed and how it was fixed.
Summarizing a PR or branch before handing it to a person.
avoidWhen: Live status of branches and plans: use ak:watzup.
Handing work to another agent: use ak:handoff.
Prioritizing next work: use ak:sowat.

params.name: [task|PR|branch|recent]
params.desc: Recap scope: a task, PR, branch, or 'recent' (resolution not documented in source).

examples.note: Recaps work done in this session.
Summarizes a PR for reviewers.

tips: It never says deployed or released without current evidence.
Output is selective; ask a follow-up for more detail.
Secrets and personal data in evidence are redacted.

ak-watzup.tagline: Status handoff from branches, worktrees, plans, and roadmaps, with ranked next steps.
ak-watzup.summary: ak:watzup scans branches, remote refs, worktrees, unfinished plans, and docs roadmaps, then reports state and 5-6 ranked next steps. It is read-only and uses the network only when you ask it to fetch.
howItWorks: Runs node scripts/watzup-scan.cjs --json; adds --fetch only when you ask to refresh remotes.
Computes plan progress from - [ ] / - [x] checkboxes in plan.md and phase-*.md.
Ranks next steps by status and current worktree/branch; hygiene issues like a dirty tree go first.
Reports Current State, Recent Work, In-Flight Plans, Roadmaps, Next Steps, Warnings.
If the scanner fails, falls back to read-only git and find commands, labeled as fallback.
useWhen: End of session: what is in progress and what comes next.
You opened a new worktree or detached checkout and need context.
You want every unfinished plan across branches with completion %.
avoidWhen: A continuation contract for an AI agent: use ak:handoff.
A recap of what was just built: use ak:sumup.
Updating plan status: use ak:project-management.

params.name: [branch|worktree|status]
params.desc: Report focus: a branch, worktree, or general status (handling not documented in source).

params.name: --fetch
params.desc: Refreshes remote refs before reporting. Use only on request; default is no network.

examples.note: Project status and next steps.
Explicit request that makes the scanner run --fetch.

tips: Without fetch, remote refs may be stale; the report warns about it.
A dirty tree is a hygiene step, never a reason to discard changes.
Plans with stale checkboxes look less complete than they are.
artifacts: Status report in chat (no file written)

ak-retro.tagline: Sprint retrospectives from git data: velocity, code health, hotspots, plan progress.
ak-retro.summary: ak:retro computes git metrics and plan progress for a time range and writes plans/reports/retro-{YYMMDD}-{slug}.md with 3-5 recommendations. It is read-only and marks missing data N/A instead of inventing numbers.
howItWorks: Parses the timeframe (7d, 2w, 1m, sprint, or a date range); --compare adds the prior equal period.
Runs scripts/collect-git-metrics.py for commit frequency, test-to-code ratio, churn, and active days.
Counts plan checkboxes in plans/ changed during the period.
Fills the report template with real data; --team splits by author, --compare adds deltas.
--format html builds a self-contained page; never commits, pushes, or edits source.
useWhen: End-of-sprint retros that need objective numbers.
Finding high-churn hotspot files before a refactor.
Comparing with the previous period or per member.
avoidWhen: Judging individual productivity: commits and LOC are descriptive only.
Summarizing a feature just built: use ak:sumup.
Current status and next steps: use ak:watzup.

params.name: [timeframe]
params.desc: Analysis window, default 7d: 7d, 2w, 1m, sprint, or YYYY-MM-DD:YYYY-MM-DD.

params.name: --compare
params.desc: Adds deltas versus the previous equal period.

params.name: --team
params.desc: Splits metrics by author.

params.name: --format html|md
params.desc: md (default) or html: a self-contained page at plans/reports/retro-{YYMMDD}-{slug}.html.

params.name: --no-antv
params.desc: Disables AntV Infographic in HTML output.

params.name: --no-diagram-design
params.desc: Disables the diagram-design layer in HTML output.

params.name: --no-editorial-visuals
params.desc: Disables all editorial visuals; overrides project and user config.

examples.note: 2-week sprint compared with the prior 2 weeks.
Quarterly review per member, as HTML.

tips: Shallow clones lack history; fetch full history for accurate numbers.
A failed git command means no evidence, not zero activity.
Test-to-code ratio uses path names, not execution coverage.

ak-plans-kanban.tagline: Open the AgentKit CLI plans dashboard: kanban, timeline, progress.
ak-plans-kanban.summary: ak:plans-kanban opens the /plans route of the dashboard built into the ak CLI (default http://127.0.0.1:8766/plans), starting it if needed. It only opens the UI; plan changes belong to ak plan.
howItWorks: Checks the ak CLI and reads ak config status --json for a running dashboard.
If none runs, starts ak config start --port 8766 --no-open --no-interactive.
Probes for plans support; on failure prints an upgrade notice and exits 1.
Opens /plans in the browser unless --no-open; legacy flags only warn.
useWhen: Seeing many plans at once as a kanban board.
Checking timelines and progress of active versus finished plans.
Showing progress to others visually.
avoidWhen: Updating plan status: use ak plan or ak:project-management.
A text status report with next steps: use ak:watzup.
Custom host or port: run ak config start directly.

params.name: --stop
params.desc: Stops the dashboard this launcher started.

params.name: --no-open
params.desc: Ensures the dashboard runs without opening a browser.

params.name: --open
params.desc: Opens the browser (default).

params.name: --dir | --plans | --port | --host
params.desc: Deprecated; ignored with a warning.

params.name: --background | --foreground
params.desc: Deprecated; ignored with a warning.

params.name: [path]
params.desc: Legacy path; ignored with a warning.

examples.note: Opens the plans dashboard, starting it if needed.
Stops the dashboard the launcher started.

tips: On 'ak not found', install the AgentKit CLI or set AGENTKIT_CLI.
A project dashboard shows only project plans; a global one shows only global plans.
Stop only the dashboard this task started.
artifacts: Dashboard process on port 8766 (if the launcher started it)

ak-project-management.tagline: Track progress, update plan status, and sync runtime tasks with plan files.
ak-project-management.summary: ak:project-management treats plan files as the source of truth and the runtime task list as a temporary view. It reports status, hydrates tasks, syncs checkboxes back, and writes pm reports; ak:cook calls it to finalize.
howItWorks: Routes to status, update, hydrate, or sync; without a live task surface, edits the plan directly.
Hydrate mirrors unchecked - [ ] items into live tasks with enough context to map back.
Checks acceptance criteria before marking anything done; unmappable tasks are never claimed complete.
Sync scans every phase file, flips checkboxes, backfills earlier phases, and updates plan.md frontmatter.
Writes {reports-path}/pm-{date}-{time}-{slug}.md and asks docs-manager to update docs when behavior changed.
useWhen: Checking overall progress of running plans.
Updating checkboxes and status after a phase finishes.
Resuming multi-phase work in a new session.
avoidWhen: Creating a plan: use ak:plan.
Implementing a plan: use ak:cook.
Visual kanban only: use ak:plans-kanban.

params.name: status
params.desc: Reports progress from plan checkboxes and frontmatter.

params.name: hydrate
params.desc: Rebuilds the live task view from unchecked plan items.

params.name: sync
params.desc: Flips finished items to [x] across all phases, backfills earlier ones, and updates frontmatter status.

params.name: report
params.desc: Writes a status report to {reports-path}/pm-{date}-{time}-{slug}.md.

examples.note: Shows progress of active plans.
After a phase finishes, syncs checkboxes and status.

tips: Losing the live task list loses no progress; plan files are the truth.
Un-backfilled checkboxes in earlier phases skew completion percentages.
Frontmatter status accepts only pending | in-progress | completed.
artifacts: Updated checkboxes and frontmatter in plans/*/plan.md and phase-XX-*.md

ak-project-organization.tagline: Fallback rules for file locations, naming, folders, and Markdown templates.
ak-project-organization.summary: ak:project-organization answers where to put files and how to name them when repo conventions are silent. Organize mode scans folders, proposes moves, and executes only after confirmation.
howItWorks: Reads repo guidance first; uses the fallback catalog only when no layout owns the file.
Folders: src/, docs/, plans/, tests/, scripts/, assets/{type}/; naming {YYMMDD-HHmm}-{slug} or evergreen {slug}.
Slugs are lowercase, hyphenated, max 50 characters; multi-file items get their own subfolder.
Organize mode: scan → propose a from → to table → confirm → move → verify.
Never overwrites files or touches .git/, node_modules/, or .env; respects .gitignore.
useWhen: Cleaning a folder with inconsistent names or misplaced files.
Structuring a new project without existing conventions.
Unsure where to save plans, reports, or assets.
avoidWhen: Repo already has clear conventions: follow them.
Writing project docs: use ak:docs.
Creating a subfolder CLAUDE.md: use ak:folder-context.

params.name: [directories or files to organize]
params.desc: Folders or files to organize; runs Organize mode (scan → propose → execute after confirmation).

examples.note: Standardizes doc names and locations.

examples.cmd: /ak:project-organization where should scout reports be saved?
examples.note: Advisory question about path and name.

tips: Git does not protect uncommitted files; review the proposal before approving moves.
Date format comes from $CK_PLAN_DATE_FORMAT, default YYMMDD-HHmm.
Code files: kebab-case for JS/TS/Python/Shell, PascalCase for C#/Java/Swift, snake_case for Go/Rust.
artifacts: Moved or renamed files and folders
New category folders, .gitkeep for empty ones

ak-ak.tagline: Operate the ak CLI safely: install, inspect, update, recover, remove kits.
ak-ak.summary: ak:ak teaches agents to use the ak CLI without damaging user state. It classifies each command's effect, confirms project or global scope, inspects first, and snapshots before recover or uninstall.
howItWorks: Classifies the goal as read-only, mutating, or diagnostic, and checks ak <cmd> --help.
Uses --json --no-interactive for scripted reads; confirms project or user/global scope and kit source.
Inspects first: ak doctor, ak kit validate, ak skill verify, ak backups list.
Runs ak backups create before recover, restore, uninstall, or --fresh; never combines --force with --fresh.
Smoke-tests installers in a temp home, never on real state; reports command, scope, and result.
useWhen: Installing, refreshing, validating, or removing an AgentKit kit.
Diagnosing installs with ak doctor or ak diagnostics export.
Recovering from a broken install with ak recover or ak backups restore.
avoidWhen: Writing or editing a skill: use ak:skill-creator.
Choosing a skill for a task: use ak:agentkit.
Writing or executing plans: use ak:plan, ak:cook.

params.name: [goal or subcommand]
params.desc: Goal or ak subcommand; exact flags come from ak <cmd> --help.

params.name: init | new | setup | onboard
params.desc: Setup commands, all mutating; ak onboard runs setup, login, then kit install.

params.name: kit
params.desc: Kit lifecycle; only list-kits and validate are read-only.

params.name: skills / skill
params.desc: ak skills for inventory; ak skill to install, repair, upgrade, or verify one skill.

params.name: plan / journal
params.desc: Read commands (list, show, status) are safe; create, check, update, archive mutate.

params.name: doctor / diagnostics / backups
params.desc: Read-only diagnostics; backups create snapshots state before mutating.

params.name: recover
params.desc: Mutating and irreversible without a prior ak backups create; confirm scope and preview first.

params.name: self-update
params.desc: Updates the binary; read ak versions and ak changelog first.

params.name: login
params.desc: Top-level auth (with logout, whoami, licenses); writes user state.

examples.cmd: /ak:ak check whether the AgentKit install has problems
examples.note: Runs ak doctor and interprets the result.

examples.cmd: /ak:ak install the engineer kit for this project
examples.note: Confirms project scope before mutating.

tips: Never invent flags: if it is not in ak <cmd> --help, it does not exist.
Always state project or global scope, adapter, and skipped conflicts.
Never rerun a mutating command for diagnostics; use --verbose on a read-only reproduction.
artifacts: Kit and skill changes in project or user scope

ak-find-skills.tagline: Find and install agent skills from the open ecosystem.
ak-find-skills.summary: ak:find-skills discovers, compares, and installs skills via npx skills and skills.sh. It runs only on an explicit request or a verified capability gap.
howItWorks: Choosing among installed AgentKit skills uses references/domain-routing.md, not the Skills CLI.
Searches with npx skills find [query] and presents name, purpose, install command, and link.
On approval runs npx skills add <owner/repo@skill>; uses -g only for a user-wide install.
If nothing fits, says so and suggests npx skills init.
useWhen: You ask "is there a skill for X?".
Comparing community skills before installing.
Checking or updating installed skills with npx skills check / update.
avoidWhen: Installed workflows already cover the request: just do the work.
Writing a new skill: use ak:skill-creator.
Installing or removing AgentKit kits: use ak:ak.

params.name: [capability or task description]
params.desc: Capability or task to search for; used as the npx skills find query.

examples.note: Finds React performance skills.

examples.cmd: /ak:find-skills which installed skill fits SEO work?
examples.note: Picks from the installed catalog via domain-routing.md.

tips: Use specific keywords: 'react testing' beats 'testing'.
Default scope is the current project; -g installs user-wide.
External skills are third-party code; check provenance before installing.
artifacts: Skill installed via npx skills add

ak-skill-creator.tagline: Create, update, audit, optimize, and package agent skills with evals.
ak-skill-creator.summary: ak:skill-creator has 4 workflows: create, update, audit (report only), and optimize (diff, applied only with --apply). It defaults to project scope and requires evidence proportional to the change before calling it done.
howItWorks: Resolves scope: kit (inside the AgentKit repo only), project (default), or user on request.
Creates a skeleton with scripts/init_skill.py, then writes outcome, constraints, and verification.
Validates with scripts/quick_validate.py and scripts/lint_cruft.py --routing; high findings are fixed or recorded.
Evidence scales with change: routing traces for metadata, baseline-vs-candidate runs for instructions.
Update bumps metadata.version; --advice consults kongming at checkpoints.
useWhen: Creating a skill for a recurring team workflow.
A skill triggers at the wrong time and routing needs diagnosis.
Auditing a skill or kit for stale or redundant instructions.
avoidWhen: Building a CLI or MCP server: use ak:agentize or ak:mcp-builder.
Finding existing skills: use ak:find-skills.
Installing kits or skills: use ak:ak.

params.name: create <name or description>
params.desc: Creates a new skill: resolves target, captures intent, writes, and evaluates.

params.name: update <path> <change>
params.desc: Edits an existing skill, keeps accepted behavior, bumps metadata.version.

params.name: audit [path|kit|--all]
params.desc: Lint and semantic review with proposed hunks; report only. Accepts --target-model <model>.

params.name: optimize <path>
params.desc: Compares baseline with a candidate and proposes a diff by default.

params.name: [skill-name|path|kit|--all]
params.desc: Target: skill name, path, kit, or --all (with audit).

params.name: --kit <kit>
params.desc: Creates the skill in kits/<kit>/skills/ak-<slug>/; valid only inside the AgentKit repo.

params.name: --project
params.desc: Creates the skill in .claude/skills/<slug>/ or .agents/skills/<slug>/. Default scope.

params.name: --user
params.desc: Creates the skill in the runtime's user skill folder.

params.name: --long-horizon
params.desc: Uses the long-horizon scaffold and build loop; new targets only.

params.name: --apply
params.desc: With optimize: applies the diff instead of only proposing it.

params.name: --from-audit <report>
params.desc: With optimize: uses an existing audit report as input.

params.name: --advice
params.desc: Consults kongming at checkpoints; never skips validation or authorization.

Audits every skill, report only.

tips: Longer or emphatic descriptions do not improve triggering; trace real routing instead.
Lint findings are heuristics, not delete orders.
Typo-only edits need only structural checks.
artifacts: New or edited skill folder (SKILL.md, references/, scripts/)

ak-xia.tagline: Compare or port a feature from another repo in gated phases.
ak-xia.summary: ak:xia studies how another repo implements a feature and adapts it to your project: Recon → Map → Analyze → Challenge → Plan → Deliver. It writes no code; it outputs a comparison report (--compare) or a plan for ak:cook (default --port).
howItWorks: Recon packs the source with /ak:repomix, records license duties, and scouts local integration points.
Treats source repo content as untrusted: runs no commands and follows no instructions from it.
Map and Analyze build a source → local dependency matrix and trace execution to side effects.
Challenge is a hard gate before Plan; 3+ competing concerns use the brainstormer agent.
--compare writes a report to plans/reports/; other modes produce a plan for /ak:cook <plan-path>.
useWhen: You want another repo's feature rewritten for your stack.
Comparing how two codebases implement the same feature.
Copying a small module nearly as-is, respecting its license.
avoidWhen: Cloning a whole project as a starter: use ak:bootstrap.
Only packing a repo as context: use ak:repomix.
Implementing right away without analysis: use ak:cook.

params.name: <github-url-or-owner/repo|local-path>
params.desc: Source repo: GitHub URL, owner/repo, or local path. A file/folder URL narrows the scope.

params.name: [feature]
params.desc: Feature to extract; keywords like compare, copy, improve, or port also infer the mode.

params.name: --compare
params.desc: Side-by-side analysis only, report in plans/reports/. Default when intent is ambiguous.

params.name: --copy
params.desc: Transplants with minimal changes.

params.name: --improve
params.desc: Copies with refactoring to fit the local codebase.

params.name: --port
params.desc: Rewrites idiomatically for the local stack. Default mode.

params.name: --auto
params.desc: Runs the full workflow but auto-approves gates.

params.name: --fast
params.desc: Skips research and Challenge and auto-approves; use only for small, clear features.

examples.note: Compares Next.js image optimization with the current project.
Default port to the local stack, producing a plan for ak:cook.

tips: Always check the source license; xia records attribution duties.
Narrow huge repos with include patterns or a folder URL.
--fast skips Challenge and may transplant an ill-fitting design.
artifacts: Repomix pack of the source repo

ak-repomix.tagline: Pack a repo into one AI-friendly file with secret checks.
ak-repomix.summary: ak:repomix packs the smallest scope that holds the needed code, keeping ignore rules and secret exclusions. It outputs a pack file (default repomix-output.xml) with file count, tokens, and secret warnings.
howItWorks: Picks the smallest scope; never packs a whole monorepo for one module.
Keeps existing Repomix config, ignore rules, and secret exclusions.
Runs a scoped pack, e.g. repomix --include "src/**/*.ts" or npx repomix --remote owner/repo.
Checks file list, token summary, and secret warnings; reuses old packs only if inputs are unchanged.
useWhen: Loading whole modules of an unfamiliar codebase into LLM context.
Auditing a third-party GitHub library without cloning.
Snapshotting a codebase at a specific revision.
avoidWhen: Finding a few relevant files: use ak:scout.
Repeated relationship queries: use ak:graphify.
Precise go-to-definition or find-usages: use ak:gkg.

params.name: [path]
params.desc: Local path to pack (default current folder), or owner/repo or URL for remote sources.

params.name: --style xml|markdown|plain|json
params.desc: Output format; default XML (repomix-output.xml).

examples.note: Packs only the payments module as Markdown for review.
Packs a remote repo for analysis without cloning.

tips: Never disable secret checks just to get output.
Check the token summary before loading the pack; oversized packs waste budget.
Use --remove-comments when only code structure matters.

ak-graphify.tagline: Build queryable knowledge graphs from code, docs, papers, and images.
ak-graphify.summary: ak:graphify builds a knowledge graph in graphify-out/ from code (local AST), media (local Whisper), and docs/images (LLM, sent to a provider). It pays off only when repeated relationship queries justify the build cost.
howItWorks: Uses native search for small lookups; refreshes only stale inputs of an existing graph.
Lists which docs and images will leave the machine and confirms before the LLM pass.
Installs with pip install graphifyy if needed; code AST and media transcription stay local.
LLM subagents add INFERRED or AMBIGUOUS edges from docs and images.
Writes graph.html, GRAPH_REPORT.md, graph.json, and a SHA256 cache; can serve graph.json over MCP.
useWhen: Asking repeated architecture and dependency questions in a large codebase.
Finding god nodes (most connected concepts) before refactoring.
Linking code with design docs across files.
avoidWhen: Looking up one function or file: use native search or ak:scout.
One-off context dump: use ak:repomix.
Sensitive docs that must not reach a provider.

params.name: [path]
params.desc: Folder to graph; defaults to the current folder.

params.name: --mcp
params.desc: (not documented in source) Serves graph.json over MCP via python -m graphify.serve; needs graphifyy[mcp].

params.name: --report
params.desc: (not documented in source) Points to GRAPH_REPORT.md: god nodes, surprising links, suggested questions.

params.name: --watch
params.desc: Rebuilds the graph incrementally on file changes.

examples.note: Graphs one service and reads GRAPH_REPORT.md.
Serves the graph over MCP for direct queries.

tips: The PyPI package is graphifyy (two y's); other graphify* packages are unrelated.
Later builds process only changed files.
Verify LLM-inferred edges against source before key decisions.

ak-gkg.tagline: Code navigation with GitLab Knowledge Graph: definitions, usages, impact.
ak-gkg.summary: ak:gkg gives IDE-like go-to-definition, find-usages, impact analysis, and repo maps via a local index queried over HTTP (localhost:27495) or MCP. References are complete for Ruby, Java, Kotlin, and partial for Python/TS/JS.
howItWorks: Checks gkg --version and reuses a fresh index and running server when present.
Reindexes only stale parts with gkg index; stops a server only if this task owns it.
Queries tools like get_definition, get_references, and repo_map over HTTP or MCP.
Impact analysis runs get_references on the symbol and reviews every call site.
For partially supported languages, cross-checks empty results with native search.
useWhen: Finding every caller before changing a signature.
Impact analysis before refactoring in Ruby/Java/Kotlin repos.
Generating a repo map from the graph.
avoidWhen: Context dumps, remote repos, or token counts: use ak:repomix.
Not a git repo: gkg needs one.
Graphs that include docs and images: use ak:graphify.

params.name: [symbol or query]
params.desc: Symbol (function, class, method) or a query such as find usages or impact analysis.

examples.note: Finds the definition and every caller before changing logic.
Lists affected call sites.

tips: Never stop another session's gkg server.
If port 27495 is busy, gkg picks another; check gkg server status.
Run gkg clean --dry-run before cleaning orphaned data.
